To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) flexible planning problems can be solved by solving a sequence of DFCSPs using the Flexible Local Changes (FLC) algorithm; 2) the resulting plans can be of varying quality and length; 3) FLC is a competitive solver for boolean planning problems.

Flexible planning is a new paradigm for planning that supports the use of soft constraints in planning, and that it is possible to solve flexible planning problems by solving a sequence of DFCSPs, using Flexible Local Changes.

(i) flexible planning problems can be solved using the Graphplan approach; and (ii) the resulting plan extraction process can be cast as solving a sequence of linked DFCSPs, which are solved using Flexible Local Changes.

extending the Graphplan framework to deal with flexible problems.
developing techniques that enable the synthesis of plans that trade-off compromises versus plan length.

the Graphplan framework can be extended to handle flexible problems in a manner that is efficient, flexible and scalable.

flexible plan synthesis is possible in polynomial time and that flexible plans can be extracted in a way that allows the tradeoff between the compromises made in the plan versus the plan length to be controlled.
